title: Choosing a clear control structure
learningObjectives: Explain choosing a clear control structure and write reusable JavaScript functions or control flow.

understand.concept: Different control structures suit different tasks. if/else handles conditions, switch handles multiple exact-value branches, for loops handle counted repetition, while loops handle repetition while a condition remains true, and for...of handles iterable values. Clarity is more important than clever compactness.
understand.whyItMatters: Choosing a suitable structure makes code easier to test and explain. Avoid forcing a problem into a loop or switch when a simple expression or function is clearer.
understand.analogy: Choose the control structure like choosing a tool: use the one that matches the shape of the task.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript execution, hoisting, and parameter evaluation follow language rules.

explain.narrative: The conditional chooses a path based on exact state, and for...of processes each task value.

examples.explanation: The conditional chooses a path based on exact state, and for...of processes each task value.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the function or control-flow result described.

practise.guidedTask: Given four small problems—grade range, menu choice, fixed count, and array values—choose a control structure for each and justify it.
practise.independentTask: Create a small program that uses the control structure or function concept. Test normal, boundary, and optional-input cases.
hints: Keep inputs explicit and return results where practical.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Choosing a clear control structure</title></head><body>
<script>const status='ready';if(status==='ready'){console.log('Start');}else{console.log('Wait');}const tasks=['Read','Practise'];for(const task of tasks){console.log(task);}</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which structure is usually clearest for processing every value in an array?
questions.explanation: for...of directly iterates over values in an iterable.

questions.prompt: What makes a function easier to reuse and test?
options: Clear inputs, focused responsibility, and explicit results
Hidden global state and unrelated side effects
A very long function with many unrelated tasks
questions.answer: Clear inputs, focused responsibility, and explicit results
questions.explanation: Focused functions with clear inputs and outputs are easier to reason about and test.
